# VS Code / Copilot

VS Code is an independent native implementation of the Holo architecture.

## Current native fit

Current VS Code custom agents (`.agent.md`) can define their own model, tools, instructions, subagent allow-list (`agents`), user visibility and model-invocation behavior. Subagents run in separate contexts. The main agent can also request an explicit model when invoking a subagent, but Holo must not use that override because model choice is human-owned.

VS Code also provides the Agents window as a macro session/worktree manager. It can host multiple independent agent sessions. If a Copilot session is started with Holo, Holo continues to delegate internally through native custom subagents.

Current VS Code builds also expose built-in browser tools through the Integrated Browser. These are native client-side tools, not an MCP requirement.

## Canonical shape

All eleven delegated canonical Holo roles are native VS Code custom agents/subagents. MCP is a capability mechanism in VS Code, not the representation of a canonical Holo role or a model-routing layer.

```text
normal Copilot session:
Holo custom agent
  -> broad project-approved native/client/MCP tool surface
  -> native custom subagent for canonical delegated roles

macro parallel work:
VS Code Agents window
  -> independent session/worktree
      -> Holo custom agent
          -> native custom subagent
```

The Agents window is not a replacement for Holo delegation. It organizes independent top-level sessions/worktrees.

The Antigravity harness has a separate documented exception that uses fixed role-specific MCP tools because its native subagent model binding cannot realize the human-owned multi-provider roster. Do not generalize that exception to VS Code.

## Expected behavior

- `holo` remains the coordinating custom agent and final integrator.
- The eleven delegated canonical roles are represented as native `.agent.md` custom agents/subagents.
- Holo should be capability-complete within the active Copilot profile/project. Do not keep a narrow hand-maintained `tools:` subset that suppresses built-in, extension or MCP capabilities already enabled for the session.
- On builds where Integrated Browser tools are enabled, Holo should receive the native browser tool group, including page navigation, content inspection, interaction and screenshot capability.
- Tool availability does not bypass VS Code approvals, workspace trust, network filtering or MCP scope.
- Give Holo the `agent` tool and an explicit `agents` allow-list containing only the native Holo subagents intended to be callable.
- Set `disable-model-invocation: true` for Holo so another model does not treat Holo itself as a delegated worker.
- Native delegated roles may be `user-invocable: false` when intended to be Holo-only workers; user visibility is a UI/product choice and must not change the role contract or model binding.
- Bind the model in each delegated agent's `model` frontmatter when the selected model is exposed through the active VS Code language-model system.
- Holo must not pass a different model to `runSubagent`/the agent tool; parent model override must not bypass the human-owned binding.
- Delegated/read-only roles must keep narrow tool sets appropriate to their contracts; Holo's broad tool access must not be inherited automatically by stricter roles.
- `project-rw` is the scoped implementation role.
- Independent auditors receive clean/minimally sufficient first-pass context.
- Skills, MCPs, hooks, AGENTS.md and workspace instructions use current VS Code native mechanisms.

## Coordinator tool authority

For Holo, the preferred behavior is the full tool catalog that the active VS Code/Copilot profile already enables for that project. Avoid a stale coordinator allow-list such as only `read`, `search`, `edit`, `execute`, `agent`, `web` and `todo` when the runtime exposes additional capabilities such as Integrated Browser.

The exact `.agent.md` realization is version-sensitive. If omitting `tools` preserves the full enabled tool catalog while retaining required subagent behavior, prefer that. If the installed build requires explicit declarations, use the current native all-enabled/default mechanism or the complete enabled runtime catalog. Do not invent unsupported wildcard syntax.

Keep `agents` constrained separately. Broad Holo tools do not mean unrestricted subagent invocation.

See `library/rules/tool-authority.md`.

## Runtime path durability

VS Code-canonical paths are only locations that the current VS Code/Copilot product/schema/documentation defines or supports for the relevant configuration object and scope. External executable/script locations referenced by MCP or helper configuration are host runtime dependencies, not VS Code-canonical paths merely because they are persistent.

Do not describe `/usr/bin/...`, `~/.local/bin/...`, `~/.local/lib/...`, `/opt/...` or another OS/Holo-selected location as canonical for VS Code without product evidence.

VS Code/Copilot MCP and Holo-owned helper configuration must not depend on temporary, cache, staging, extracted-download or session-specific filesystem paths.

Reject commands/interpreters under `/tmp`, `~/tmp`, disposable `/var/tmp`, `~/.cache`, Downloads extraction directories, one-off build folders or transient mount/runtime paths. A setup-time path is not a valid persistent MCP dependency.

For MCP `command` values and helper launchers, prefer a stable executable name through the Agent Host's verified `PATH` or a persistent absolute path discovered on the actual machine when an absolute path is required. Do not hardcode a versioned Node/Python/toolchain extracted into scratch space.

After changing a path, reload/restart the affected MCP and prove the Agent Host starts it from the intended stable location. Validate configuration placement and runtime dependency separately. See `library/rules/canonical-runtime-paths.md`.

## Reasoning effort

Reasoning configuration is version-sensitive. Builds that support `reasoning-effort` in custom `.agent.md` files should persist the human-owned reasoning level there. Builds that do not support it may require session/UI reasoning selection.

`reasoning-effort` controls the model's reasoning depth/effort; it does not change tools, permissions, provider availability or context isolation. Higher effort may improve difficult reasoning but usually costs more latency/tokens. Preserve the roster intent without treating reasoning effort as a permission mechanism.

When unsupported by the installed build, classify that part of the binding as manual/unverified rather than pretending the model name alone makes the binding exact.

## Model availability

A canonical VS Code role remains a native custom agent even when its selected model is temporarily unavailable from the active VS Code language-model providers.

Do not turn that role into a model-routing MCP tool merely to bypass provider availability. Instead:

- inspect the currently installed VS Code language-model providers and model picker;
- bind the human-selected model in the role's `.agent.md` when it is exposed;
- if the selected model cannot currently be bound, report that role binding as unavailable/manual for this harness;
- never silently inherit Holo's model, substitute another model, or introduce a generic model router.

MCP servers in VS Code remain external capability/data integrations used by Holo or delegated agents as appropriate. They are not the canonical role identity or model-selection mechanism.

## Agents window and worktrees

The Agents window is useful when the human wants multiple independent large sessions, especially with worktree isolation. Starting Holo inside a session must preserve Holo's internal delegation rules; the user should not have to select specialist models manually for each role whose binding is available.

Use separate worktrees for parallel write-heavy sessions that might overlap. A worktree is code isolation, not a security boundary; preserve the harness's normal permission/sandbox policy.

Do not use the Agents window merely to emulate focused subagents. Focused delegation belongs inside Holo via the native `agent` mechanism.

## Applying or updating

Before changing VS Code configuration:

1. inspect the installed stable/Insiders version and selected agent harness;
2. inspect the current `.agent.md` schema, profile-wide enabled tool catalog and available language-model providers;
3. identify which VS Code/Copilot locations are actually defined/supported for the configuration objects being changed; do not invent VS Code-canonical runtime directories;
4. verify Holo receives the full project-approved tool catalog, including Integrated Browser when enabled, without disabling native approval/trust controls;
5. represent all eleven canonical delegated roles as native custom agents/subagents;
6. bind each role to its human-owned model through the native VS Code language-model system when available, otherwise report the binding limitation rather than converting the role into MCP model routing;
7. verify Holo's `agents` allow-list, `disable-model-invocation`, each delegated role's narrow tool set, model and reasoning behavior;
8. audit all Holo-owned MCP/interpreter/helper executable paths as runtime dependencies and reject ephemeral/cache/staging references;
9. smoke-test Holo with a current native capability such as Integrated Browser and native delegated roles from the roster;
10. verify a Holo session launched from the Agents window still delegates internally without manual role/model switching for available bindings;
11. preserve unrelated workspace settings, extensions, authentication and provider state.

Follow `library/rules/harness-freshness.md`, `library/rules/tool-authority.md`, `library/rules/canonical-runtime-paths.md` and `library/rules/session-orchestration.md`.

Implement semantic Holo invariants with the current native features. Do not generate VS Code configuration from another harness.

# Zed

Zed is an independent native implementation of the Holo architecture.

## Current native fit

Current Zed Agent supports Agent Profiles with a default model plus selectable built-in and MCP tools, native Skills, MCP servers, parallel threads/worktrees, and `spawn_agent` subagents with isolated context. Zed also provides `agent.subagent_model` to choose the model used by spawned subagents.

Two current limitations matter for Holo:

1. `spawn_agent` subagents receive the same tools as the parent; and
2. `agent.subagent_model` is a shared subagent-model setting, not a separate per-canonical-role model binding.

Therefore `spawn_agent` alone cannot faithfully realize the full Holo roster and least-privilege boundaries.

That limitation does **not** make Zed another Antigravity-style MCP-role harness. The current Holo specification allows role-specific MCP model routing only for the explicit Antigravity exception. Zed should preserve native behavior and report any per-role binding limitation rather than converting canonical roles into MCP model wrappers.

## Preferred Holo shape

```text
normal thread:
Zed Agent / Holo profile
  -> broad project-approved native tools/Skills/context servers
  -> uses native spawn_agent only where shared model/tools are semantically acceptable
  -> reports explicit limitation/manual workflow where a canonical per-role binding cannot be represented

macro parallel work:
Zed parallel thread/worktree
  -> Holo profile
      -> same native semantics and limitations
```

- Use one primary Holo-oriented Zed Agent profile for the interactive coordinator.
- The Holo profile should expose the built-in tools, Skills and context-server tools approved for the active project/profile rather than a small coordinator-only subset.
- Preserve project/workspace context-server scoping and worktree trust; capability-complete does not mean enabling every global context server everywhere.
- Do not require the user to switch profile/model/thread for every canonical role as if that were automatic Holo delegation.
- Do not create one Zed profile per Holo role merely to imitate Kilo unless the human explicitly chooses a manual profile workflow.
- Do not use `spawn_agent` as a canonical role when its inherited toolset or shared `subagent_model` would violate that role's model/permission contract.
- Do not create fixed role-specific MCP model-routing tools merely to force full roster parity.

## Coordinator tool authority

Holo is the coordinator and final integrator, so least privilege should not be implemented by suppressing normal project-approved Zed capabilities from the Holo profile.

When a built-in tool, Skill or context-server tool is enabled for the active project/profile, Holo should be able to choose it directly. Native approval/trust behavior remains in force.

Delegated canonical roles remain narrower. Native `spawn_agent` must not be used to impersonate a strict role when it would inherit Holo's broader tool surface or the wrong shared model.

See `library/rules/tool-authority.md`.

## Runtime path durability

Zed-canonical paths are only locations that the current Zed product/schema/documentation defines or supports for the relevant configuration object and scope. External executable/script locations used by `context_servers` or helpers are host runtime dependencies, not Zed-canonical paths merely because they are persistent.

Do not describe `/usr/bin/...`, `~/.local/bin/...`, `~/.local/lib/...`, `/opt/...` or another OS/Holo-selected location as canonical for Zed without product evidence.

Zed `context_servers`, external-agent launchers and Holo-owned helper scripts must not depend on ephemeral filesystem locations.

Reject paths under `/tmp`, `~/tmp`, disposable `/var/tmp`, cache/staging directories, Downloads extraction directories, one-off build outputs, transient mounts or session-specific runtime directories. Do not point Zed at a versioned interpreter/runtime extracted into scratch space as a persistent dependency.

Prefer a stable executable name resolved through Zed's verified launch `PATH`, or a persistent absolute path discovered on the actual machine when Zed requires one. Project-owned scripts are acceptable when their lifecycle is intentionally tied to that persistent project.

After changing any context-server command/interpreter/helper path, restart or open a fresh Zed Agent thread where possible and verify the server starts from the intended stable location. Validate configuration placement and runtime dependency separately. See `library/rules/canonical-runtime-paths.md`.

## Native `spawn_agent`

`spawn_agent` remains useful for temporary parallel investigations where:

- the shared subagent model is appropriate;
- inheriting the parent's available tools is acceptable; and
- the spawned worker is not being represented as a stricter canonical Holo role.

For example, Holo may use native Zed subagents for opportunistic same-model research/parallel context collection. Do not label such a worker `bug-auditor`, `architecture-auditor`, `project-ro` or another canonical role unless its effective model and authority actually match that role.

If there is no clearly safe/useful generic-worker case for the current Holo profile, `spawn_agent` may be omitted/disabled from that profile rather than widening authority.

## Profiles

Agent Profiles control default model and tool availability for a Zed Agent thread. Profiles are useful for the Holo coordinator and for human-selected alternative working modes, but profile switching is not the canonical automatic delegation mechanism for the multi-model Holo roster.

Historical multi-profile Holo layouts should be consolidated when they existed only to compensate for older Zed limitations. Preserve unrelated user profiles.

The main Holo profile should not be used as the place to enforce delegated-role least privilege.

If the human explicitly wants a manual per-profile workflow for a particular project, that is a user-selected working mode, not automatic Holo role routing.

## Model-binding limitation

When the human-owned canonical role model cannot be represented through current native Zed subagent semantics, do not silently inherit the Holo/session model and do not create a model-routing MCP wrapper.

Instead:

- record the canonical role/model binding from `library/routing/model-bindings.yaml`;
- inspect whether the current Zed build gained a native per-subagent or per-role model/tool mechanism;
- if not, classify automatic realization of that role as limited/manual for Zed;
- keep generic native subagents separate from canonical role identity;
- revisit the implementation when Zed gains a faithful native mechanism.

This limitation is preferable to importing the explicit Antigravity MCP-role exception into another harness without human approval.

## Skills, MCP and parallel work

Zed supports native Skills. Do not classify Zed as globally unsupported for Skills; inspect whether each desired Skill is actually installed/discoverable and record `present`, `missing` or `unknown` accordingly.

MCP servers remain external capabilities/data sources used through Zed's context-server mechanism. They are not canonical Holo role identities or model routers.

Use Zed worktrees when parallel threads may edit overlapping files. Parallel threads/worktrees are a macro isolation layer, not a replacement for role routing inside Holo.

External Agents and Terminal Threads are useful human-controlled alternatives, but they are not an automatic replacement for Holo role routing unless the user explicitly chooses that workflow.

## Applying or updating

1. inspect the installed Zed stable/preview version and current settings schema;
2. inspect `agent.profiles`, `agent.subagent_model`, MCP servers, Skills and tool permissions;
3. identify which Zed locations are actually defined/supported for the configuration objects being changed; do not invent Zed-canonical runtime directories;
4. keep one Holo coordinator profile rather than a manual one-profile-per-role workflow by default;
5. verify the Holo profile exposes the full built-in/Skill/context-server capability surface approved for the active project/profile, without globally enabling unrelated context servers;
6. audit all Holo-owned context-server/interpreter/helper paths as runtime dependencies and reject ephemeral/cache/staging references;
7. use native `spawn_agent` only where its shared model/tool inheritance is semantically correct;
8. do not introduce fixed role-specific MCP model-routing tools; report any canonical per-role model/authority limitation instead;
9. verify the actual model and operational authority of any native delegated worker before representing it as a canonical role;
10. verify Holo can run inside a normal or parallel Zed thread/worktree without silently substituting models;
11. smoke-test one direct native Holo capability, safe native subagent behavior where configured, stable context-server startup and Skill discovery;
12. preserve unrelated settings, credentials, external-agent configuration and provider state.

Follow `library/rules/harness-freshness.md`, `library/rules/tool-authority.md`, `library/rules/canonical-runtime-paths.md` and `library/rules/session-orchestration.md`.

Zed does not need structural parity with Kilo, VS Code or Antigravity. Its faithful Holo implementation should exploit current Zed Agent features, report native limitations honestly, and avoid importing Antigravity's MCP-role exception.

`library/` contains architecture semantics, not deployable harness configuration.

- `agents/` defines the canonical role instructions.
- `routing/model-bindings.yaml` records the human-owned reference model roster.

# Architecture Auditor

Perform an independent read-only audit of contracts, boundaries, security,
integrations, migrations, resilience, and systemic risk. Check data flows,
trust boundaries, coupling, failure modes, and operational assumptions against
explicit requirements.

For the first independent assessment, work from the artifact under review,
architecture/contracts, diff/code, migrations, deployment evidence, tests,
logs, traces, and other objective evidence. Do not accept another model's
conclusion, rationale, confidence, or proposed fix as framing before forming
your own assessment.

If the explicit task is later to confirm or refute a prior finding, treat that
finding as a hypothesis to test against the artifact and evidence, not as ground
truth.

Do not modify implementation, schemas, migrations, or configuration. Treat
absence of evidence as uncertainty and return findings to the coordinator.

violations, boundary conditions, and error paths. Report findings first, ranked
by impact and evidence, with exact locations and reproduction steps where
possible.

applicable requirements, diff/code, tests, logs, traces, and other objective
evidence. Do not accept another model's conclusion, rationale, confidence, or
proposed fix as framing before forming your own assessment.

truth.

and dashboards. Validate definitions and data quality, make investigations
reproducible, and distinguish facts from hypotheses.

without a separate explicit authorization. Treat inaccessible or missing data
as uncertainty, not success.

# Explore

Act as a read-only context worker for repository and workspace exploration. Find relevant files, symbols, references, dependency paths and nearby instructions, then return a compact evidence map to the caller.

This role is intentionally designed for economical, fast models such as Gemini Flash or DeepSeek Flash. The exact model is selected by the human in `library/routing/model-bindings.yaml`; never choose or substitute a model yourself.

Do not make final debugging or architecture decisions. Do not edit files. Minimize context pollution: return only relevant paths, locations, relationships, notable observations and unresolved questions.

# Final Gate

Make the final read-only decision from requirements, verification, independent
audits, and residual risk. Return exactly one of `PASS`, `CORRECT`, `BLOCK`, or
`INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE`, with blocking findings and evidence gaps.

Fail closed on missing evidence. Do not modify implementation or status and do
not infer deployment, completion, or safety from silence.

PATH: library/agents/holo/instructions.md

# Holo

Act as the coordinating primary agent and final integrator for the assigned work. Understand scope, read applicable project instructions, gather enough context, plan proportionally to risk, implement or coordinate the approved change, and verify before handoff.

Work alone by default. Delegate only when specialization or context isolation is useful. Select the **role** to call; never select or substitute a model yourself. The human-owned mapping in `library/routing/model-bindings.yaml` determines which model occupies each role. If the selected model cannot be expressed or reached in the current harness, report that harness limitation rather than silently substituting another model.

Plan from the goal to the required capability before choosing a concrete tool name. For delegated work, choose the canonical role whose contract best matches the goal. For direct execution, inspect the MCPs/tools and Skills actually exposed by the current harness/project and select the least-privileged concrete capability that satisfies the need.

Do not assume a tool or Skill exists because it exists in another harness or appears as a conceptual capability in the architecture. When the needed capability is unavailable, state the limitation and continue only with an evidence-preserving alternative that remains inside the role's authority.

Use Skills when their procedure or domain knowledge is relevant to the task; do not load Skills merely because they are available. Treat Hooks as harness lifecycle automation: account for their effects and avoid duplicating them, but do not select Hooks as ordinary discretionary tools unless the harness explicitly exposes a manual action.

Use `explore`, `shell` and `browser` as economical context workers when repository search, command output or web/documentation exploration would otherwise pollute the main context. Treat their output as collected evidence, not final authority.

Prefer observable environment evidence over unsupported inference. If a claim can be checked against files, command output, tests, logs, browser state, documentation or a project data source, use the available capability to obtain that ground truth before asserting the claim.

For substantive specialist results, require a handoff that identifies the claim, concrete evidence, verification performed or proposed, and uncertainty or unresolved risk. Analyze the returned evidence before acting. Verify proportionally to impact: a focused inspection or test is enough for many low-risk claims; consequential or uncertain findings may justify an independent reviewer.

Do not repeat a specialist's entire investigation by default, and do not call multiple models merely to create consensus. Escalate only when evidence is insufficient, specialists conflict, or the change is high risk.

Remain responsible for accepting, rejecting or escalating findings and for the final integrated change. Before claiming success, inspect the final diff/state and run the checks that materially support the claim. Never treat absence of errors, model reputation, or an unsupported PASS as evidence.

# Shell

Act as a scoped command-execution context worker. Run only bounded, non-destructive commands authorized by the caller, then condense terminal output into useful evidence.

This role is intentionally designed for economical, fast models such as DeepSeek Flash or Gemini Flash. The exact model is selected by the human in `library/routing/model-bindings.yaml`; never choose or substitute a model yourself.

Do not turn command output into an unsupported root-cause or architecture conclusion. Report the command, exit status, relevant output, failures and any uncertainty. Avoid returning large raw logs when a faithful concise summary plus the decisive lines is sufficient.

Never perform destructive resets, credential operations or unrelated environment changes unless explicitly authorized by the governing project policy.

# Test Engineer

Act as an independent specialist for tests, regressions, coverage, and edge
cases. Identify behavior that needs regression protection, inspect existing
gaps, design focused tests, and report reproducible failures with residual risk.

# Antigravity 2.0 project-scope policy

This rule applies to the standalone Antigravity 2.0 desktop application.

Current Antigravity 2.0 uses Projects as the primary isolation boundary. Projects have their own folders, security settings and permissions, but reusable MCP servers are managed from global Customizations. Do not assume the Antigravity CLI/IDE workspace-local `.agents/mcp_config.json` behavior is the native MCP-definition scope of the standalone 2.0 Project surface.

## MCP definitions

For Antigravity 2.0 desktop:

- reusable MCP servers are installed/managed globally through Settings -> Customizations -> Installed MCP Servers;
- global enable/disable is a server-management control, not a per-project activation map;
- project settings and permissions remain project-scoped;
- MCP permission rules can target a whole server or a specific tool using `mcp(server/*)` or `mcp(server/tool)`.

Therefore Holo must not move Antigravity 2.0 desktop MCP definitions into `.agents/mcp_config.json` merely to imitate CLI, IDE, Kilo, VS Code or Zed scoping.

## Desired Holo behavior

When a server is globally installed but only some Projects need it:

1. keep the reusable server definition in the native global Antigravity 2.0 customization store;
2. use Project-level permissions to restrict or allow its MCP tools for the Projects that need them when the installed 2.0 build exposes those permission controls;
3. keep unnecessary project grants absent or denied/ask according to the human's desired security posture;
4. do not claim the server is project-local if it is still globally installed/discovered;
5. do not introduce a custom MCP registry, proxy, loader, synchronizer or wrapper only to simulate per-project installation.

This reduces effective authority per Project even though Antigravity 2.0 currently manages reusable MCP definitions globally. It may not remove globally installed servers from the tool discovery catalog; report that product limitation honestly.

## Holo role MCP tools

The fixed UCP/OpenCode role MCP tools needed by the Antigravity Holo architecture may remain globally installed because they implement the harness itself rather than a single application's domain integration. Their invocation is still constrained by Holo role semantics and Project permissions where applicable.

Domain MCPs such as PostgreSQL, Laravel, Firebase, n8n, Grafana, Sentry, Jupyter or deployment-specific tools should not receive broad global allow permission merely because the server is installed globally. Grant them only in the Projects that need them when possible.

## Product distinction

Do not conflate these surfaces:

- Antigravity 2.0 desktop: Project-centric; reusable MCPs managed globally; Project settings/permissions are isolated.
- Antigravity CLI: supports global `~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json` and workspace-local `.agents/mcp_config.json`.
- Antigravity IDE: can use global or workspace-local MCP config.

Always identify the active product surface before applying MCP scope rules.

# Delegation and Evidence

Holo delegates by role, not by model identity. The human-owned model binding is resolved outside the role definition.

## Default

Work alone when delegation adds little value. Delegate when specialization, independent review, parallel isolation or context protection materially improves the task.

## Context Workers

`explore`, `shell` and `browser` are low-cost context workers. They should normally use economical, fast models such as Gemini Flash or DeepSeek Flash, with the exact binding chosen by the human. Their job is collection and condensation, not final judgment.

## Specialist Handoff

A substantive delegated result should preserve these semantic fields:

- `claim`: concise conclusion or hypothesis;
- `evidence`: concrete files/lines, commands, tests, logs, sources or observations;
- `verification.performed`: checks already executed;
- `verification.proposed`: checks that would confirm or falsify the claim;
- `uncertainty`: confidence, assumptions and unresolved risks.

A model reputation or unsupported assertion is never sufficient evidence.

## Independent Audit Context

For an independent audit, the first assessment must be made from the artifact under review, applicable requirements/contracts, and objective evidence such as diffs, tests, logs, traces, or observed runtime state.

Do not prime an independent auditor with another model's conclusion, rationale, confidence, proposed fix, or claim that the implementation is correct or incorrect before its first assessment.

After the auditor has formed its own assessment, a prior finding may be supplied for explicit confirmation, falsification, reconciliation, or root-cause investigation. In that case, treat the prior finding as a hypothesis to test, not as ground truth.

This is context isolation for review, not an additional mandatory gate. Do not add duplicate reviewers merely to satisfy this rule.

## Holo Review

Holo reviews the evidence and verifies proportionally to risk. Do not repeat the entire investigation by default. Prefer the cheapest independent check that can materially confirm or falsify the claim.

- low risk: focused inspection, diff or relevant test;
- medium risk: evidence review plus targeted verification;
- high risk: independent reviewer plus targeted verification;
- critical: independent evidence, project checks, final gate and Holo integration.

Do not call multiple models merely to manufacture consensus.

## Architecture And Root Cause

Treat root-cause analysis as a hypothesis until supported by reproduction, falsification or another concrete causal check. Treat architecture findings as recommendations until Holo evaluates evidence, alternatives, impact and project constraints.

## Final Gate

The final gate checks existing evidence, verification and unresolved risk. It is not an oracle and must not return a meaningful PASS without supporting evidence.

# Harness freshness and support classification

Harness capability claims are version-sensitive. Never treat a prior local inventory, an old documentation snapshot, or another harness's behavior as sufficient evidence for the current runtime.

## Required inspection order

Before applying Holo to a harness or classifying one of its capabilities:

1. identify the installed harness version/build actually in use;
2. inspect the current native configuration/schema exposed by that installed build;
3. check current official documentation/release notes for the relevant capability;
4. distinguish what the product supports from what is currently configured on this machine;
5. verify behavior locally when a cheap smoke test can settle the question.

If the public product has gained a capability that the installed build does not yet have, record that as a version gap. Do not call the capability globally unsupported.

## Status discipline

Use capability states carefully:

- `present` — observed configured locally; this does not imply a full runtime smoke test unless separately stated.
- `missing` — the current harness supports a useful equivalent, but it was not found in the inspected local configuration.
- `broken` — configured locally, but a required file/reference/runtime dependency is invalid.
- `unknown` — support or local presence has not been verified sufficiently.
- `unsupported` — after checking the installed version and current product behavior/docs, there is no useful equivalent for the desired capability.
- `not-desired` — the human explicitly does not want that capability on this harness.

`unsupported` is a strong conclusion. Absence from local configuration is normally `missing` or `unknown`, not `unsupported`.

## New native mechanisms

If a harness adds a better native mechanism, prefer it over an older workaround when doing so preserves Holo semantics. Do not keep manual profile switching, inherited-model subagents, custom wrappers, or other historical adaptations merely because they were previously configured.

A current native mechanism may still be unsuitable for a canonical Holo role if its effective model, tools, authority, context isolation, or audit independence do not match the role contract. In that case report the limitation or manual requirement unless the human has explicitly approved a harness-specific adaptation in this specification.

Do not invent a role-specific MCP model-routing fallback merely because native model binding is missing or inconvenient. The current explicit MCP-as-role exception is Antigravity and is defined in `harnesses/antigravity.md`. Any new exception requires a deliberate specification change.

## Evidence in documentation

When updating `harnesses/` or `capabilities/roster.yaml`, record the observation date/source when practical and avoid timeless statements about fast-moving product features unless they are architectural invariants.

Architecture is canonical; support claims are observations and must be refreshed when runtimes change.

# MCP scope policy

MCP servers should be scoped as narrowly as practical. Project-specific capabilities belong in project/workspace configuration when the current harness supports that scope; global MCP configuration is reserved for capabilities intentionally useful across most projects or required by the harness itself.

## Default rule

Prefer this order:

1. project/workspace-local MCP configuration;
2. project-specific profile/tool/permission enablement where the harness supports it;
3. global MCP configuration only for broadly reusable capabilities or when the product surface requires global server management.

Do not enable every known MCP globally merely because it exists in the capability roster. Extra MCP servers and tools increase context/tool-selection noise, startup/runtime overhead, permission surface, and accidental cross-project access.

A capability roster entry records desired/observed availability, not that the server must be globally active in every project.

## Project examples

A project that does not use PostgreSQL should not receive PostgreSQL MCP authority merely because another project needs it. Likewise, Laravel-specific, Firebase-specific, n8n-specific, Grafana, Sentry, Jupyter, browser automation, or deployment MCPs should normally be project-scoped or project-restricted unless the human intentionally wants them everywhere.

Broadly useful personal MCPs such as documentation/search providers may remain global when the human prefers that convenience, but this is a user choice rather than an architectural requirement.

## Harness-specific realization

### Kilo

Use project `kilo.json[c]` or `.kilo/kilo.json[c]` for project-specific MCP entries. Global `~/.config/kilo/kilo.json[c]` is only for MCPs intentionally available in all projects. Project configuration takes precedence over global configuration.

### VS Code / Copilot

Prefer workspace `.vscode/mcp.json` or workspace `.mcp.json` for project MCPs. Use user-profile MCP configuration only for servers intentionally shared across workspaces. When the VS Code Agents window/Agent Host is used, ensure the chosen workspace-level form is actually forwarded/read by that harness build.

### Antigravity 2.0 desktop

Antigravity 2.0 standalone is Project-centric, but current product documentation states that reusable MCP servers are managed globally through Settings -> Customizations -> Installed MCP Servers. Projects have isolated settings and permissions, not an independent reusable-MCP installation store.

Therefore:

- do not move Antigravity 2.0 desktop MCP definitions into workspace `.agents/mcp_config.json` merely to simulate project scoping;
- keep reusable server definitions in the native global customization store;
- use Project-level permissions to narrow effective MCP authority with `mcp(server/tool)` or `mcp(server/*)` where the installed build exposes those controls;
- do not give domain MCPs broad global allow permission unless the human wants them globally trusted;
- report honestly that a globally installed server may still remain globally discoverable even when Project permissions restrict its use.

The fixed Holo UCP/OpenCode role MCPs may remain globally installed because they implement the Antigravity Holo harness itself rather than one application's domain integration.

See `library/rules/antigravity-2-project-scope.md`.

### Antigravity CLI / IDE

Do not conflate these with standalone Antigravity 2.0. Current CLI/IDE documentation supports workspace-local `.agents/mcp_config.json` in addition to global `~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json`; use workspace-local scope there when appropriate.

### Zed

Prefer project `.zed/settings.json` `context_servers` for project-specific MCPs. Keep global `~/.config/zed/settings.json` MCPs only for intentionally universal servers. Zed worktree trust applies to project settings that can start MCP servers, so project MCPs may require the worktree to be trusted before activation.

Agent Profiles should also expose only the MCP tools appropriate to the active Holo profile/project; `enable_all_context_servers` should not be used merely for convenience when a narrower set is known.

## Secrets

Project-level MCP configuration may be committed to source control. Do not place literal credentials in repository files. Use the harness's supported environment-variable, keychain, OAuth, secret-file, or input mechanism. Preserve existing authenticated provider state.

## Applying to Holo

When applying Holo locally:

- inspect which MCPs each project actually needs;
- move Holo-managed project-specific MCP definitions out of global scope when the harness natively supports project scope;
- on Antigravity 2.0 desktop, keep reusable MCP definitions global but narrow Project permissions rather than inventing workspace-local installation semantics;
- do not move unrelated user-managed global MCPs without explicit human intent;
- avoid duplicate global + project definitions unless the harness requires them;
- smoke-test project activation/permission behavior and verify that unrelated projects do not receive unintended MCP authority;
- preserve role-specific Holo MCP tools at the narrowest scope that still allows the Holo implementation to function.

Project scoping is a capability/permission optimization, not a new routing layer. Do not add a universal MCP registry, synchronizer, installer, or cross-harness generator to enforce it.

# Session orchestration and delegated roles

Holo distinguishes macro session/worktree orchestration from ordinary role delegation.

A session manager is not a Holo role and does not replace role delegation. It organizes independent top-level workspaces, worktrees, or long-running agent sessions. Holo still coordinates the work inside each session using that harness's normal delegation mechanism.

## General rule

Use a session/worktree manager when a unit of work would naturally justify its own branch/worktree or independent long-running session. Use ordinary role delegation for focused exploration, testing, diagnosis, audit, implementation, or review inside a session.

Do not create extra sessions merely to simulate subagents. Do not allow multiple write-capable sessions to edit the same working tree concurrently.

Role-specific MCP model routing is not a generic delegation mechanism. The current explicit exception is Antigravity; other harnesses should use their native delegation mechanisms and report native binding limitations instead of importing the Antigravity exception.

## Kilo

Kilo Agent Manager is a macro orchestration layer. A user may open Agent Manager, create a session/worktree, select Holo as the agent, and give Holo a large objective. Inside that session Holo continues to use the `task` tool to invoke the canonical custom subagents.

Canonical shape:

```text
Kilo Agent Manager
  -> independent session/worktree
      -> Holo primary
          -> task -> canonical subagent
```

Agent Manager is optional. It is best for independent large features, competing approaches, or long-running work that benefits from branch/worktree isolation. It is not the default mechanism for `explore`, audits, focused root-cause work, or small implementations.

## VS Code

The VS Code Agents window is also a macro session manager. A user may open a Copilot session/worktree using the Holo custom agent. Holo then delegates internally through the native custom-agent/subagent mechanism.

Canonical shape:

```text
VS Code Agents window
  -> independent session/worktree
      -> Holo custom agent
          -> native canonical custom subagent
```

All eleven canonical delegated Holo roles remain native VS Code custom agents. The Agents window may also host other harnesses, but those sessions are independent. Do not treat another harness session as a Holo subagent unless the user explicitly chooses such a workflow.

## Zed

Parallel Agent threads/worktrees are macro isolation tools. A Holo profile inside a thread continues to use current Zed-native tools and safe `spawn_agent` workers where semantically appropriate.

Current Zed native subagent model/tool semantics may be insufficient to realize every canonical per-role binding automatically. When that happens, report the limitation or manual workflow rather than importing Antigravity-style fixed role MCP model routing.

## Antigravity

Antigravity's Holo implementation is the explicit current exception: it does not use native Holo subagents for the canonical roster. Separate Antigravity sessions may still be used by the human for independent work, but role delegation inside a Holo session remains MCP-based through fixed role-specific tools.

# Coordinator and delegated tool authority

This rule defines the capability boundary between the Holo coordinator and delegated roles.

## Core policy

Holo is the primary coordinator and final integrator. Within the capabilities that the current harness, active project/workspace, trust state, user profile and MCP scope already make available, Holo should be **capability-complete** rather than artificially restricted to a small static tool allow-list.

Delegated roles are different: they should remain **least-privileged** according to their canonical contracts.

Conceptually:

```text
HOLO
  -> broad access to project-approved harness capabilities
  -> may read, edit, execute, browse, use Skills/MCPs/tools and delegate when useful
  -> still subject to host approvals, trust, project scope and human policy

DELEGATED ROLE
  -> only the tools/capabilities required by that role
  -> read-only roles stay effectively read-only
  -> nested delegation denied unless explicitly required
```

Broad capability does **not** mean automatic approval. A tool may be available to Holo while the harness still asks the human before sensitive execution. Tool availability, tool approval and project/MCP scope are separate controls.

## What remains restricted on Holo

Capability-complete Holo does not mean unrestricted routing authority.

Preserve all of these invariants:

- Holo selects roles, not models;
- human-owned model/provider/reasoning bindings remain authoritative;
- Holo must not silently substitute, fall back to, or inherit a different model for a delegated canonical role;
- Holo's delegated-agent allow-list remains restricted to the canonical roles intended for that harness;
- project-specific MCPs remain project/workspace scoped where the harness supports it;
- globally installed MCPs that are not approved for the active project do not become automatically available merely because Holo is capability-complete;
- host trust, approval, sandbox and sensitive-file controls remain active;
- no generic model router, cross-harness dispatcher or universal capability resolver is introduced.

## Delegated-role least privilege

Native subagents and other delegated workers receive only the authority their role requires. Antigravity's fixed role MCP tools are the explicit current harness exception and must preserve the same least-privilege intent.

Examples:

- `explore`: read/search/context inspection only;
- `shell`: bounded command execution appropriate to the assigned task;
- `browser`: browser/web inspection capabilities plus only the local read context it needs;
- `bug-auditor`, `architecture-auditor`, `final-gate`, `project-ro`: read-only effective authority;
- `test-engineer`: test execution and evidence gathering without unrelated write authority unless explicitly required by the contract;
- `project-rw`: write/execute only inside the explicit delegated scope.

A delegated role must not inherit Holo's broad tool authority merely because the harness supports inheritance. If the native mechanism cannot preserve the role boundary, report the limitation unless an explicit harness-specific exception has been approved in the specification. Do not create a new model-routing MCP role implicitly.

## Holo direct work versus delegation

Holo may use any project-approved capability directly when delegation would add little value. Delegation exists for specialization, independent review, context isolation, cost control or useful parallelism; it is not required merely because a specialized tool exists.

This means, for example, that Holo may use a native integrated browser directly for a quick visual check while still delegating a larger browser investigation to the canonical `browser` role when isolation or specialization helps.

## Harness realization

### Kilo

Do not deny ordinary Kilo tools to Holo merely to make the coordinator least-privileged. Holo should be able to request the tools/MCPs/Skills available in the active project, while normal Kilo approval rules may still ask before sensitive actions.

Keep `permission.task` special: deny by default and allow only the eleven canonical Holo subagents. Delegated subagents keep role-specific permissions and nested `task` denied by default.

### VS Code / Copilot

Do not maintain a narrow hand-curated `tools:` list on Holo that suppresses newly available built-in or extension capabilities. Holo should receive the full tool catalog enabled for the active Copilot profile/project, including native Integrated Browser tools when the installed build exposes them.

If the current `.agent.md`/Agent Host schema requires explicit tool declarations for the selected target, use the current native mechanism that means "all enabled tools" or derive the complete enabled catalog from the runtime; do not preserve a stale subset such as only `read`, `search`, `edit`, `execute`, `agent`, `web` and `todo`.

Keep the `agents` allow-list restricted to the intended native Holo subagents. Broad tool access does not imply broad subagent access.

All eleven delegated canonical Holo roles are native custom agents/subagents in VS Code. MCP servers remain capability/data integrations, not role/model-routing substitutes. If a selected role model is unavailable through the active VS Code language-model providers, report the binding limitation instead of converting that role into an MCP wrapper.

### Antigravity

Holo remains the only native Holo agent. Give that main Holo agent the native tools and MCP capabilities approved for the active Project. Project permissions continue to narrow effective authority even when reusable MCP definitions are globally installed.

The eleven canonical delegated roles remain fixed role-specific MCP tools with their own least-privileged operational authority and fixed model/provider bindings. Do not turn Holo's broad authority into a generic model bridge or pass it through to audit/read-only role tools.

### Zed

The main Holo Agent Profile should receive the built-in tools, Skills and context-server tools approved for that project/profile instead of a small coordinator-only subset. Preserve project-level context-server scoping and worktree trust; capability-complete does not mean enabling every globally configured context server in every project.

Use Zed-native delegation only where the shared subagent model and inherited tool surface are semantically compatible. Do not import Antigravity-style role-specific MCP model routing into Zed to force roster parity. When a canonical per-role model/tool boundary cannot be expressed by the current Zed native mechanism, report that limitation or manual workflow explicitly.

## Validation

After applying this rule to a harness, verify both sides of the boundary:

1. Holo can see and use the currently enabled project-approved capabilities, including newly added native capabilities such as browser tools when present;
2. Holo's agent/subagent routing allow-list remains constrained;
3. delegated roles still expose only their role-appropriate tools/authority;
4. read-only roles cannot edit or execute destructive actions;
5. project-specific MCPs have not been widened to unrelated projects;
6. sensitive actions still follow the harness's native approval/trust policy;
7. no model fallback, inherited-role model substitution or generic router was introduced.

The invariant is:

`Holo is capability-complete inside the project's approved harness surface; delegated roles are capability-minimal inside their contracts.`
